chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who performed li'an against his wife while she was pregnant and her pregnancy had clearly become apparent, and he denied what was in her womb. Then when she gave birth, he claimed the child, acknowledged him, and alleged that he was from him.
So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "His child is returned to him, and he inherits from him, and he is not flogged, because the li'an has already passed."

key_terms.اسْتَبَانَ حَمْلُهَا: her pregnancy had become clearly visible
key_terms.اللِّعَانَ: the legal procedure of mutual imprecation between spouses
key_terms.لَا يُجْلَدُ: he is not subjected to flogging
key_terms.لَاعَنَ امْرَأَتَهُ: he invoked li'an against his wife through mutual cursing
key_terms.وَلَدُهُ: his child, legally ascribed to him here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man performs li'an and later acknowledges the child after the birth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a man who denied the child in his wife's womb through li'an and then later acknowledged the child after birth. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the child is ascribed back to him and inherits from him, while the man is not flogged because the procedure of li'an had already been completed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5697 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who had invoked li'an against his wife while she was pregnant, and her pregnancy was visibly apparent. He denied what was in her womb.
However, after she gave birth, he claimed the child and acknowledged it, asserting that it was his.
Abu Abdullah (as) said: "The child is returned to him, and he inherits from him, and the man is not subjected to flogging because the li'an has already taken place."
